chunks: Jamīl ibn Darrāj asked him about a mutamatti‘ who shaved his head in Makkah, so he said:

"If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him. If he did that intentionally during the first thirty days of the months of hajj, then there is nothing upon him. But if he did that intentionally after the thirty days in which the hair is left to grow for hajj, then a blood sacrifice is upon him which he must spill."

key_terms.الثَّلَاثِينَ: the thirty-day period mentioned for letting the hair grow
key_terms.الشَّعْرُ: the hair that is to be left for hajj
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: acting out of ignorance of the ruling
key_terms.شُهُورِ الْحَجِّ: the months designated for hajj rites
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: he sheds it, meaning he offers the required sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mutamatti‘ who shaves his head in Makkah before hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamatti‘ who shaves his head in Makkah before hajj. It distinguishes between ignorance and deliberate action, and between an earlier and later period before hajj, with a blood sacrifice required only in the latter intentional case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2750 - Jamil ibn Darraj asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a person performing tamattu‘ who shaved their head in Mecca.

Imam (as) said: "If it was done out of ignorance, there is no penalty upon them. If they intentionally did so during the first thirty days of the months of Hajj, there is also no penalty. However, if they intentionally did so after the thirty days, during which the hair is to be preserved for Hajj, they must offer a blood sacrifice."
